intro: Two of the league's best young players went down this week, with Drake Maye out for the Patriots and Aidan Hutchinson done for the Lions. Sunday brings the first international Sunday Night Football game, as the 49ers and Vikings meet in Mexico City. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Drake Maye fractures his ankle and is likely done for the Patriots
top.dek: The Patriots have only said Maye will miss the Week 12 game at the Chargers. Adam Schefter reports he will likely miss most or all of the season. Tommy DeVito is expected to take over for a team still facing Buffalo, Kansas City, Minnesota and Denver.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Lions lose Aidan Hutchinson for the season before Tampa Bay visits
top.dek: Hutchinson went down on the play where he sacked Maye in Munich, and he is out for the year. Rookie Derrick Moore, with four sacks in his last two games, will carry more of the pass rush. Center Cade Mays is also out Sunday, and safety Kerby Joseph is set to debut.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Mahomes throws five touchdowns as Chiefs rout Falcons 35-13
top.dek: Patrick Mahomes went 22 of 35 for 348 yards and five scores. Kansas City moved to 7-2 and tied Denver for first in the AFC West. Josh Downs caught a touchdown in his first game as a Chief.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 45-0: Bears' first-quarter margin over their last four games
top.dek: Chicago has outscored four straight opponents by that score in the opening period. The Bears rank fourth in rushing at 142.0 yards per game. The flip side is 17 turnovers, tied for fifth-most in the league.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: 49ers and Vikings play the first international Sunday Night Football game
top.dek: San Francisco (8-1) meets Minnesota (7-2) at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City on Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. The stadium sits at roughly 7,500 feet, so watch how both teams handle the altitude.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills hold the No. 1 seed, warn of Miami

stories.text: Bills ride a five-game win streak into Miami week
stories.summary: Buffalo is 8-1 and holds the top seed in the AFC. Josh Allen told reporters the Dolphins are hungry and that Sunday is no cake walk, and offensive coordinator Joe Brady said he does not like the word winnable. The Bills host Kansas City on Thanksgiving, so they have little room to coast.

stories.text: Benford and Williams out, Kincaid doubtful vs. Miami
stories.summary: Cornerback Christian Benford (groin) and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) are out, and rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr will start in Williams' place. Tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb, ankle) is doubtful. Safety Damar Hamlin, tight end Jackson Hawes and lineman T.J. Sanders are questionable.

stories.text: James Cook has scored in eight of nine games
stories.summary: Cook has 971 rushing yards on 5.2 yards per carry and nine touchdowns. He has found the end zone in every game except the opener in Houston. Buffalo has 20 rushing touchdowns as a team, more than it has thrown.

stories.text: 10, 6, 12: points the Bills defense allowed in three straight
stories.summary: The Bills gave up 30 or more points four times in their first six games. Over the last three they have held opponents to 10, 6 and 12. Buffalo is also scoring 31.9 points per game.

stories.text: Dolphins visit Buffalo Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Buffalo hosts Miami on Sunday, November 22, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. ESPN lists the Bills as 16.5-point favorites. Watch the secondary, which is thin with Benford out, against a Miami offense starting Kyle McCord.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins start McCord at Buffalo, eye top-3 pick

stories.text: Dolphins at 1-8 start McCord against Buffalo
stories.summary: Miami will start Kyle McCord against a Bills team that has beaten several backup quarterbacks lately. The Dolphins appear headed for a top-three pick in the 2027 draft, and local coverage is already debating quarterback versus pass rusher. Buffalo is a 16.5-point favorite.

stories.text: Brewer questionable, Trader doubtful for Buffalo
stories.summary: Center Aaron Brewer is in concussion protocol and practiced fully Friday, so he is expected to play if he has no symptoms. Safety Dante Trader Jr. did not practice all week and is doubtful, and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee) is also doubtful. Punter Bradley Pinion and receiver Jared Wayne are out.

stories.text: Malik Washington leads Miami's receivers at midseason
stories.summary: Washington tops the Dolphins in both receptions and receiving yards. Miami Herald columnist Chris Perkins named him the team's midseason MVP. Rookie Chris Bell, a year removed from a torn ACL, is the receiver the staff still wants to see break out.

stories.text: 320.6: yards per game the Dolphins defense allows
stories.summary: That mark ranks 10th in the NFL, even with Miami at 1-8. The group has lost several defensive tackles for the season, and Kenneth Grant is expected to lead what is left. Buffalo's rushing attack will test it right away.

stories.text: At Buffalo Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Miami visits the Bills on Sunday, November 22, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch how Kenneth Grant and the interior line handle James Cook, and whether Brewer is cleared at center.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Maye's fractured ankle clouds Patriots' bye

stories.text: Drake Maye fractured his ankle, likely out for the year
stories.summary: Multiple reports say Maye has a fractured ankle. The Patriots have said only that he will miss the Week 12 game at the Chargers, while Adam Schefter reports he will likely miss most or all of the season. Tommy DeVito is expected to take over, and New England still faces Buffalo, Kansas City, Minnesota and Denver.

stories.text: A.J. Brown hurts hamstring, Henderson goes to IR
stories.summary: Receiver A.J. Brown left the Lions game in the second half with a hamstring injury, one game after he returned from ankle and knee problems. Running back TreVeyon Henderson went on injured reserve with a neurological issue. Coach Mike Vrabel does not expect Maye back when the team returns from the bye.

stories.text: Christian Gonzalez gets his first interception
stories.summary: Gonzalez picked off a pass in Munich for his first of the season. Safety Kevin Byard also intercepted one, his second game in a row with a pick. Gonzalez signed a four-year, $135 million extension in September.

stories.text: 494: yards the Patriots defense gave up to Detroit
stories.summary: That is the most New England has allowed this season in the 35-10 loss. The defense has surrendered 400 or more yards and 30 or more points in each of its last four losses. Vrabel blames execution.

stories.text: Bye week, then at Chargers Nov. 29, 4:05 p.m. ET
stories.summary: New England is off this week. The Patriots visit the Chargers on Sunday, November 29, at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS, after the NFL flexed the game out of Sunday night. The quarterback plan is the question to watch.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Geno Smith set to play at Chargers

stories.text: Geno Smith is on track to start at the Chargers
stories.summary: Smith hurt his left ankle in the 31-12 loss to Buffalo, and coach Aaron Glenn said he remains the starter. He was a full participant in Friday's practice and carries no game designation. The Jets have lost five straight, and rookie Cade Klubnik is the fallback.

stories.text: Cooper, Williams and Onyemata out at Los Angeles
stories.summary: Receivers Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle, hip) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) and lineman David Onyemata (abdomen) are out. Edge Joseph Ossai, lineman Harrison Phillips, linebacker Trevin Wallace and guard Dylan Parham are questionable.

stories.text: Cade Klubnik made his NFL debut in relief
stories.summary: The fourth-round rookie from Clemson came on against Buffalo and completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards with one interception. He took three sacks. He would make his first start if Smith cannot go.

stories.text: 135: rushing yards per game the Jets defense allows
stories.summary: That ranks 30th in the NFL. The Chargers have Omarion Hampton, who ran for 105 yards in their Week 10 win over Baltimore. The Jets offense is scoring 19.4 points per game, 26th.

stories.text: At Chargers Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Jets visit the Chargers on Sunday, November 22, at 4:05 p.m. ET on Fox. Los Angeles is 1-8 and ranks last in scoring at 16.0 points per game. Watch whether the Jets can slow the run.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens drop a fifth straight to winless L.A.

stories.text: Ravens lose a fifth straight to a Chargers team that had no wins
stories.summary: Los Angeles beat Baltimore 23-20 on Monday night for its first win of the season, and the Ravens fell to 4-6. It is their longest losing streak since 2021. A late strip of Zay Flowers ended the comeback chance with about two minutes left.

stories.text: Madubuike, Humphrey and Hawkins out at Carolina
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring), cornerback Marlon Humphrey (personal) and safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) are out Sunday. Lamar Jackson will miss the game as well, and Brissett starts again at quarterback.

stories.text: Brissett throws for 340 yards in his Ravens debut
stories.summary: Brissett completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards and one interception against the Chargers. Mark Andrews posted season highs with eight catches for 82 yards. Derrick Henry scored twice, moving into seventh place on the NFL career touchdown list.

stories.text: 16: rushing yards on 15 carries against the Chargers
stories.summary: Baltimore had six first-half carries for zero yards, the fewest in team history. The Chargers ran for 160 yards on the Ravens, the most any opponent has gained on them this season.

stories.text: Ravens visit the Panthers on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Carolina is 4-5 and leads the NFC South. The Panthers beat New Orleans 20-17 on a last-second field goal, and Chuba Hubbard had 172 yards from scrimmage. Watch whether Baltimore can run the ball with Henry after last week's 16-yard day.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Burrow's MVP push heads to Monday night

stories.text: Burrow brings an MVP case to Monday night in Washington
stories.summary: Joe Burrow has four total touchdowns in five straight games and threw for 300 yards in the first half against Pittsburgh. Cincinnati throws on 64.4 percent of its snaps, the highest rate in the league, and the Bengals sit at 7-2.

stories.text: Burrow practices fully through an illness
stories.summary: Burrow was a full participant Thursday and Friday with an illness and said he will be at full strength Monday. Guard Dalton Risner (knee), linebacker Oren Burks (groin) and cornerback Dax Hill (illness) did not practice. No Bengal carries an official game designation yet.

stories.text: Chase can match Calvin Johnson's streak of 10-catch games
stories.summary: Ja'Marr Chase can tie Calvin Johnson's record of four straight games with 10 or more receptions on Monday. He and Tee Higgins have combined for 189.9 yards per game this season.

stories.text: 64.4%: Bengals pass rate, the highest in the NFL
stories.summary: Cincinnati has gone back to a shotgun, pass-first offense. Burrow has thrown seven touchdowns on deep passes, second in the league, and completes more than 74 percent of his throws between 10 and 19 yards.

stories.text: Bengals at Commanders on Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET on ABC and ESPN
stories.summary: Washington is 3-5-1 and blitzes on about 41 percent of snaps, a top-five rate. Burrow completes over 70 percent of his passes against the blitz. Former Commanders tackle Jonathan Allen faces his old team.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns rest up after another big comeback

stories.text: Browns erase a 17-point hole and head into their bye at 6-4
stories.summary: Cleveland beat Houston 27-24 after trailing 17-0. It was the Browns' fourth double-digit comeback win this year, the most in franchise history. Week 11 is the bye, and the staff now has a 10-game sample to study.

stories.text: Bye gives Fannin, Concepcion and Boston time to heal
stories.summary: Tight end Harold Fannin Jr. and receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston each left the Houston game in pain and returned. The Browns listed 12 players on the Week 10 injury report, and the week off gives them time to recover.

stories.text: Watson throws for 312 yards against his old team
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson completed 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards and ran for a season-high 49 yards against Houston. He joined Joe Flacco and Josh McCown as the only Browns quarterbacks with three straight 300-yard starts. Jerry Jeudy added a 65-yard catch.

stories.text: -72: Cleveland's first-quarter point differential
stories.summary: That is the worst first-quarter mark in the NFL, and the Browns have scored only 13 first-quarter points. They have also allowed 42 sacks, the most in the league, and often have to rally late.

stories.text: Browns host the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: The league flexed the Week 12 game into Sunday Night Football at Huntington Bank Field. Las Vegas starts rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. The Browns' defense has not allowed a 300-yard passer in 55 straight games.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers face a Hurts-less Eagles team

stories.text: Steelers travel to a depleted Eagles team without Hurts
stories.summary: Philadelphia is 2-7 on a seven-game losing streak, and Jalen Hurts is on injured reserve with blood clots in his lungs. Joe Milton starts at quarterback. Pittsburgh is a 4.5-point favorite at 6-3.

stories.text: Six Steelers questionable, Herbig the biggest worry
stories.summary: Linebacker Nick Herbig (hip, ribs) did not practice all week. Pittman (foot), Roman Wilson (hand) and guard Gennings Dunker (knee) are still in their 21-day windows and need activation to play. Patrick Queen and DeShon Elliott were full on Friday.

stories.text: Jaylen Warren is the engine at 5.7 yards a carry
stories.summary: Warren has 719 rushing yards on 126 carries, plus 30 catches for 320 yards. DK Metcalf leads the receivers with 35 catches for 432 yards. Philadelphia ranks last in the league in yards per game.

stories.text: 26: sacks taken by Aaron Rodgers through nine games
stories.summary: Rodgers has 2,014 passing yards, 15 touchdowns and six interceptions with an 86.4 passer rating. T.J. Watt has 7.5 sacks on the other side of the ball.

stories.text: Steelers at Eagles on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The game is at Lincoln Financial Field. Watch whether Pittsburgh activates Pittman and Wilson from injured reserve, and how the line holds up with left guard Mason McCormick out with an ankle injury.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans rout Colts for first home win

stories.text: Texans smother Colts 26-3 for first home win
stories.summary: Houston lost its first four home games, then beat Indianapolis on Thursday night behind three touchdown passes from C.J. Stroud. The defense added a safety and a blocked field goal. The Texans moved to 4-6 and next play Baltimore on Nov. 29.

stories.text: Braswell carted off, Houston waits on test results
stories.summary: Defensive end Chris Braswell hurt his right leg on the opening kickoff and left on a cart with the leg in a vacuum splint. The team has given no diagnosis or timeline. Houston already lacks Danielle Hunter, and Sheldon Rankins (ankle) and Kayshon Boutte (hip) also carry injuries into the Ravens game.

stories.text: Stroud hits three touchdown passes for a third straight game
stories.summary: Stroud threw for 194 yards and three scores against Indianapolis: 42 yards to Nico Collins, 24 to Kayshon Boutte and 13 to rookie Marlin Klein. He has thrown at least three touchdown passes in each of his last three games. He said afterward the team needs to build on it with a run.

stories.text: 11.5: Will Anderson Jr.'s league-leading sack total
stories.summary: Anderson sacked Daniel Jones in the end zone for a safety in the third quarter, pushing Houston's lead to 19-3. His 11.5 sacks lead the NFL.

stories.text: Ravens visit Houston on Sunday, Nov. 29
stories.summary: The Texans host Baltimore on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET, with CBS carrying the game in Houston. Watch how the defensive line holds up if Braswell is out and Hunter stays sidelined, and whether the run game repeats its 167-yard day.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts cut Daniel Jones, turn to Richardson

stories.text: Colts release Daniel Jones, name Richardson the starter
stories.summary: Indianapolis cut Jones a day after he was benched in a 26-3 loss to Houston. Coach Shane Steichen said Jones did not ask for the release. Anthony Richardson Sr. starts Nov. 29 against the Giants, his first start since 2024. Jones signed a two-year, $88 million deal in March and finished with 13 interceptions, the most in the league.

stories.text: Colts lose McGowan to a hamstring and play without both tackles
stories.summary: Running back Seth McGowan hurt his hamstring on Thursday and did not return in the second half. Both starting offensive tackles were already out, and the secondary and offensive line carry further injuries. Indianapolis now has a bye to heal before the Giants.

stories.text: Rookie C.J. Allen leads everyone with 16 tackles
stories.summary: Allen made 16 tackles against Houston, the most of any player in the game. The rookie put up the number while the offense gave the defense little rest, running for only 38 yards on 17 carries.

stories.text: 17: straight drives without a Colts touchdown
stories.summary: Indianapolis has gone 17 consecutive possessions without reaching the end zone. Spencer Shrader hit a 34-yard field goal Thursday, missed from 56 and had a 62-yarder blocked. The Colts have lost six of their last seven.

stories.text: Giants visit Lucas Oil Stadium on Nov. 29
stories.summary: Indianapolis is on its Thanksgiving week bye, then hosts the New York Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The Giants were 5-3-1 entering Week 11. Watch Richardson's accuracy and how the patched offensive line holds up.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars chase the AFC's top seed

stories.text: Jaguars beat Titans 40-23 to reach 7-2
stories.summary: Trevor Lawrence threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns as Jacksonville won its fifth straight over Tennessee, a franchise record. The win keeps the Jaguars in the chase for the AFC's No. 1 seed.

stories.text: Hainsey misses practice, Monheim moves to center
stories.summary: Center Robert Hainsey (knee) did not practice Thursday, and Coach Liam Coen said Jonah Monheim will start at center. Nine others were limited, including Travon Walker (rib), Jakobi Meyers (ankle) and Antonio Johnson (ankle). BJ Green (forearm) practiced fully.

stories.text: Parker Washington posts a career-high 152 yards
stories.summary: Washington caught seven passes for 152 yards and a 2-yard touchdown against Tennessee, his team-high sixth score of the season. His score came on the Jaguars' first possession.

stories.text: +125: Jacksonville's league-best scoring margin
stories.summary: NFL.com's Week 11 picks panel points to a point differential of plus 125 for Jacksonville, the best in the league, and all five analysts pick the Jaguars at the Giants. Jacksonville is 7-2.

stories.text: At Giants on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Jacksonville visits MetLife Stadium to face New York (5-3-1). J.J. McCarthy is starting at quarterback for the injured Jaxson Dart. Watch whether the Jaguars can protect Lawrence with Monheim at center.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans sink to 1-8 after Jaguars loss

stories.text: Titans fall to 1-8 after 40-23 loss to Jaguars
stories.summary: Tennessee gave up 40 points at home and is still winless at Nissan Stadium in its final season there. Jacksonville has now beaten the Titans five straight times. Cam Ward kept the offense moving, but the defense could not get stops on third down.

stories.text: Five Titans listed questionable for Dallas
stories.summary: Safety Tony Adams (concussion), linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. (neck), cornerback Micah Robinson (hip), running back Tyjae Spears (knee) and receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) are questionable. Guard Fernando Carmona Jr. (ankle) is out. All five questionable players practiced fully on Friday.

stories.text: Cam Ward throws a career-long 50-yard completion
stories.summary: Ward went 28 of 39 for 231 yards, two touchdowns and one interception against Jacksonville. His 50-yard throw to Elic Ayomanor is the longest completion of his career. He found Daniel Bellinger and Tony Pollard for scores.

stories.text: 535: Cam Ward's passing yards over two games
stories.summary: Ward has completed 68 percent of his passes for 535 yards, four touchdowns and one interception over his last two games. Dallas ranks last in run defense, which also plays into Ward's scrambling.

stories.text: At Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tennessee travels to AT&T Stadium to face Dallas (4-6). The Cowboys moved defensive play-calling from Christian Parker to Mike Pettine. Watch Ward's legs and Tony Pollard against a defense in flux.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos return from bye to face a rising Raiders team

stories.text: Broncos come off the bye wary of a changed Raiders team
stories.summary: Denver sits at 7-2 and shares first place in the AFC West with Kansas City. Sean Payton told reporters this Las Vegas team looks different from the ones Denver beat the last two years, and the Raiders have played the Chiefs, Seahawks and Bills to one-score games. The Broncos are 4-0 against Las Vegas over two seasons and see the Raiders twice in the next five weeks.

stories.text: Brandon Jones questionable, Lohner out for Raiders game
stories.summary: Safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) practiced on a limited basis all week and carries a questionable tag. Tight end Caleb Lohner (foot) is out. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, cornerback Riley Moss and safety Talanoa Hufanga all finished the week as full participants and have no game status.

stories.text: Rookie Jonah Coleman scores in back-to-back games
stories.summary: Running back Jonah Coleman ran 57 yards and scored from 9 yards out in the 26-21 win at Carolina, his second straight game with a rushing touchdown. Wide receiver Pat Bryant also returned from injured reserve that day and caught a 25-yard score to put the game out of reach.

stories.text: 16: straight one-score wins, an NFL record
stories.summary: The win in Charlotte stretched Denver's record streak of regular-season victories in one-score games to 16. Nik Bonitto closed it with a strip-sack of Bryce Young with 1:24 left, and the Broncos' fifth straight win moved them to 7-2 before the bye.

stories.text: Raiders visit Mile High on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Denver hosts Las Vegas Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS at Empower Field at Mile High. The Raiders allow 28.9 points per game, 31st in the league, while Denver gives up 20.7, ninth. Watch whether Denver's pass rush can pressure rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, who went down six times last week.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs share the AFC West lead after a 35-13 rout

stories.text: Mahomes throws five touchdowns as Chiefs beat Falcons 35-13
stories.summary: Kansas City moved to 7-2 and tied Denver for first in the AFC West. Patrick Mahomes went 22 of 35 for 348 yards and five scores. Josh Downs, acquired from Indianapolis earlier in the week, caught an 18-yard touchdown in his first game as a Chief.

stories.text: Trey Smith, Kenneth Walker and Jaylon Moore out vs. Cardinals
stories.summary: Guard Trey Smith (concussion), running back Kenneth Walker (groin) and tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) did not practice Friday and are out. Defensive linemen Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) and Peter Woods (neck) are questionable after limited work. Travis Kelce and Mahomes practiced fully.

stories.text: Rookie Emmett Johnson piles up 171 yards in first start
stories.summary: Johnson started in place of the injured Kenneth Walker and ran 22 times for 101 yards. He added six catches for 70 yards and two touchdowns, and forced 10 missed tackles. He now has 519 scrimmage yards, second among rookies.

stories.text: 5: games with 30-plus points in nine tries this season
stories.summary: Kansas City has scored 30 or more points five times through nine games, after doing it three times in all of last season. The Chiefs rank second in total offense and third in scoring defense, and only Chicago and Jacksonville also sit in the top 10 in all four major team categories.

stories.text: Cardinals visit Arrowhead Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The 3-7 Cardinals come to Arrowhead Stadium Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, also streaming on Paramount+. Kansas City is trying to hold a share of the division lead with Denver. Watch how the Chiefs' offensive line holds up without Trey Smith and Jaylon Moore.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Mendoza and Raiders chase a win at Denver

stories.text: Mendoza shows promise, but Seattle sacks him six times
stories.summary: Rookie Fernando Mendoza went 11 of 13 for 90 yards in the first half of his first NFL start and ran for a 10-yard score. He went 6 of 16 in the second half as Seattle rallied for a 21-13 win. Eleven Seahawks defenders pressured him over the game.

stories.text: Brock Bowers questionable with ankle and quad injuries
stories.summary: Tight end Brock Bowers sat out Wednesday, then practiced on a limited basis Thursday and Friday. He is questionable, as is kicker Matt Gay (hip). Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (stinger) is out. Bowers leads the team with 50 catches for 676 yards.

stories.text: Maxx Crosby is a half sack from a career mark
stories.summary: Crosby needs 0.5 sacks to reach 75.0 for his career. Few players drafted in the fourth round or later, or undrafted, have matched his mix of sacks, quarterback hits and tackles. He faces a Denver offense that ranks 30th in total yards per game.

stories.text: 28.9: points per game the Raiders allow, 31st in the NFL
stories.summary: Las Vegas gives up 28.9 points per game and 385.1 yards per game, which ranks 30th. Denver allows 20.7 points per game, ninth. The Raiders' offense averages 25.1 points, tenth in the league, but runs for only 70.7 yards per game, 31st.

stories.text: Raiders at Broncos Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Las Vegas visits Denver Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS, coming off two straight losses. Head coach Klint Kubiak and several staff members have past ties to Denver. Watch whether Mendoza can handle a Broncos pass rush with 26 sacks this season.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Chargers finally win, host the Jets next

stories.text: Chargers end 0-8 skid with 23-20 win at Baltimore
stories.summary: Los Angeles won for the first time this season on Monday Night Football. Justin Herbert threw a season-low 18 passes and ran in a 22-yard touchdown on the opening drive. Tarheeb Still forced a Zay Flowers fumble that Elijah Molden recovered with about two minutes left. It was the Chargers' first win since Week 16 of last year.

stories.text: Ladd McConkey questionable with back injury vs. Jets
stories.summary: Receiver Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable, along with tight end Charlie Kolar (concussion) and tackle Trey Pipkins III (knee). Linebacker Daiyan Henley (knee) is out. Khalil Mack and Donte Jackson came off the report and are fine to play.

stories.text: Omarion Hampton runs for 105 yards in the win
stories.summary: Hampton carried 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown at Baltimore, a 4.8-yard average. Herbert added 51 rushing yards, and the Chargers finished with a season-high 160 on the ground as a team.

stories.text: 16: rushing yards Baltimore managed on 15 carries
stories.summary: The Chargers held the Ravens to 16 yards on the ground, the third-lowest total by an opponent since 1990. Derrick Henry gained 10 yards on 10 carries, though he scored two touchdowns. Baltimore had zero rushing yards in the first half.

stories.text: Jets visit SoFi Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Chargers host the 2-8 Jets Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX at SoFi Stadium, opening a two-game homestand against the AFC East. New York has lost five straight. Watch whether Los Angeles can lean on the run game again.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Pettine takes over a defense in free fall

stories.text: Pettine takes over Cowboys defensive play calling
stories.summary: Senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine now calls the plays, and Christian Parker stays on as coordinator. The move follows a 46-40 loss to San Francisco. Dallas ranks 32nd in yards allowed per game and 30th in points allowed. Sunday against Tennessee is Pettine's first game as a play caller since 2020.

stories.text: Bland and Booker out, five more Cowboys questionable
stories.summary: Cornerback DaRon Bland and guard Tyler Booker are out for Tennessee. Receiver Jonathan Mingo, safeties Juanyeh Thomas and P.J. Locke, tight end Jake Ferguson and edge rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku are all listed questionable. Dallas leaves the 49ers game with a thin secondary and a reshuffled offensive line.

stories.text: Prescott keeps throwing as the defense keeps giving
stories.summary: Dak Prescott threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns against San Francisco. He has 2,724 passing yards, 21 touchdowns and six interceptions through 10 games, and he has thrown a touchdown pass in every game. He has accounted for 22 of Dallas's 32 offensive touchdowns.

stories.text: 584: yards the 49ers piled up in Arlington
stories.summary: San Francisco gained 584 yards in Week 10, the most ever at AT&T Stadium and the fourth most in franchise history. The Cowboys allowed 46 points in the 46-40 loss. Dallas sits last in the league in total yards allowed per game through 10 weeks.

stories.text: Sunday vs. Titans, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Dallas hosts 1-8 Tennessee at AT&T Stadium and has not won back to back games this season. The Cowboys need pressure on the Titans' quarterback and protection for Prescott without Booker. Thursday's game against Philadelphia follows on a short week.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants blow a lead and host Jacksonville

stories.text: Giants lose a fourth-quarter lead to Washington
stories.summary: New York fell 24-21 on Thursday night after J.J. McCarthy threw an interception to Rasul Douglas on the late drive. It was the Giants' first blown fourth-quarter lead of the season. They still lead the NFC East at 5-3-1, but Washington holds the head-to-head tiebreaker.

stories.text: Giants list no game designations for Jacksonville
stories.summary: No Giant carries an Out, Doubtful or Questionable tag. Tight end Isaiah Likely did not practice Friday with a groin issue. Safety Elijah Campbell and cornerback Nic Jones were limited with knee injuries. Cam Skattebo, Malik Harrison and Deonte Banks practiced fully.

stories.text: Isaiah Likely turns McCarthy's targets into touchdowns
stories.summary: Likely caught 9 of 11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown against Washington, including a 66-yard score. In McCarthy's three starts he has 16 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns. His seven touchdown catches lead all tight ends.

stories.text: 6: field goals rookie kicker Zvada has missed since Week 5
stories.summary: Dominic Zvada missed his only field goal try last week, a 33-yarder. All six misses came from the right hash, and coach John Harbaugh has pointed to his plant leg. The Giants also signed returner Xavier Gipson from the Eagles' practice squad this week.

stories.text: Sunday vs. Jaguars, 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The league flexed the game from 1 p.m. to the late window at MetLife Stadium. Jacksonville arrives 7-2 on a three-game winning streak behind Trevor Lawrence, who has 21 touchdowns and five interceptions. The Jaguars' defense has 12 interceptions, third most in the league.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Milton starts again as Eagles chase a win

stories.text: Eagles stay with Joe Milton at quarterback
stories.summary: Milton makes his second straight start Sunday against Pittsburgh. Philadelphia has lost seven in a row since Jalen Hurts went down for the season with blood clots. Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards in his first start, a 19-11 loss to the Giants, and led the team with 64 rushing yards.

stories.text: Baun out, DeVonta Smith cleared for Steelers
stories.summary: Linebacker Zack Baun is out with a back injury and is expected to miss multiple games. Receiver Dontayvion Wicks is also out, and linebacker Smael Mondon is doubtful. DeVonta Smith practiced fully Thursday and Friday and is cleared after a hamstring issue. Running back Will Shipley is questionable.

stories.text: Rookie Makai Lemon leads a thin receiver room
stories.summary: Lemon leads Philadelphia with 37 catches for 312 yards. He carried the passing game while DeVonta Smith missed three games. Smith's return should shift defensive attention in a week when the offense needs any help it can find.

stories.text: 4.3: yards per play, last in the NFL
stories.summary: The Eagles average 4.3 yards per play and 16.4 points per game, 30th in the league. They score on 25.5 percent of their drives, the lowest rate in the NFL. Their quarterbacks have thrown for 807 yards since Week 6.

stories.text: Sunday vs. Steelers, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Pittsburgh visits Lincoln Financial Field at 6-3. The Eagles have won every game after a bye under Nick Sirianni, and they hold an 11-game home winning streak over the Steelers. Philadelphia plays Dallas on Thursday after this one.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Daniels rallies Washington past the Giants

stories.text: Daniels survives two picks to beat the Giants
stories.summary: Jayden Daniels threw two fourth-quarter interceptions, then drove Washington down the field for a 32-yard touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs in a 24-21 win. Daniels finished 23 of 33 for 249 yards and three touchdowns. The win moved Washington to 3-5-1, and it holds the head-to-head tiebreaker on New York.

stories.text: Commanders get Croskey-Merritt and Patrick back
stories.summary: Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt practiced fully Friday for the first time since going on injured reserve Oct. 19. Center Lucas Patrick cleared the concussion protocol, and Jayden Daniels was full with his left elbow. Safety Quan Martin and running back Rachaad White were limited. Receiver Treylon Burks did not practice.

stories.text: Sonny Styles keeps stacking tackles
stories.summary: The rookie linebacker has 80 tackles on the season. He and Arvell Reese each made 13 tackles against the Giants, and Styles made a key stop late in the win. Washington's defense will lean on him again against a Bengals offense that leads the league in passing.

stories.text: 31st: Washington's rank in pass defense
stories.summary: The Commanders allow 244.8 passing yards per game, 31st in the league. Monday's opponent, Cincinnati, leads the NFL at 298.8 passing yards per game. Joe Burrow has 2,795 yards and 27 touchdown passes.

stories.text: Monday vs. Bengals, 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Washington hosts Cincinnati on Monday Night Football at Northwest Stadium and wears its all-black Hail Raiser uniforms. A win would give the team consecutive victories over the Bengals for the first time since 1985. Washington's third-down offense ranks 30th at 33.3 percent.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears win four straight but still lack a division win

stories.text: Bears sit 7-2 with an 0-2 division mark
stories.summary: Chicago has won four straight and holds the No. 6 seed in the NFC. The Bears have not beaten an NFC North team yet, and Detroit is up on Thanksgiving, four days after the Saints game. Two of the four wins came after the Jeffery Simmons trade.

stories.text: Kyler Gordon out against the Saints
stories.summary: Cornerback Kyler Gordon will miss Sunday's game with a shoulder injury he suffered in the Week 9 win over Tampa Bay. He did not practice all week. Receiver Zavion Thomas (ankle) is questionable, while running back Kyle Monangai (toe) returns after five missed games. Simmons practiced fully and plans to play.

stories.text: Jeffery Simmons is already the voice of the defense
stories.summary: Chicago sent two first-round picks to Tennessee for the defensive tackle on Oct. 29. He recorded a sack in each of his first two games and spent the bye week learning Dennis Allen's scheme. He listed a knee issue this week but says he feels fine.

stories.text: 45-0: Bears' first-quarter margin over four games
stories.summary: Chicago has outscored its last four opponents 45-0 in the first quarter. The Bears also rank fourth in rushing at 142.0 yards per game. The flip side is 17 turnovers, tied for fifth-most in the league.

stories.text: Saints at Soldier Field on Sunday
stories.summary: Chicago hosts New Orleans (3-6) on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. The Saints rank 27th in rushing offense and 27th in run defense, so watch whether Monangai and the ground game control the day.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions lose Hutchinson, lead the North at 7-2

stories.text: Lions beat Patriots in Munich, then lose Hutchinson
stories.summary: Detroit won its fifth straight, 35-10 over New England, but defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore his right ACL on the play where he sacked Drake Maye. He is out for the season. Rookie Derrick Moore, with four sacks in his last two games, is expected to carry more of the pass rush.

stories.text: Cade Mays out, Kerby Joseph set to debut
stories.summary: Center Cade Mays is out with an ankle injury, and six players are questionable: D.J. Reed, Joe Bachie, Khalil Dorsey, Tyler Lacy, Ennis Rakestraw Jr. and Sione Vaki. Safety Kerby Joseph is expected to make his season debut after a long knee rehab. Linebacker Jack Campbell is dealing with a severe neck injury.

stories.text: Jahmyr Gibbs runs wild in Munich
stories.summary: Gibbs ran for 153 yards and two touchdowns against New England and added seven catches for 99 yards. Jared Goff threw for 303 yards and three scores, and Amon-Ra St. Brown caught two touchdowns on four receptions.

stories.text: 4: Goff interceptions in his last three games
stories.summary: Goff threw no interceptions in the first six games of the season. He has thrown four in the three games since, two of them in Munich. Tampa Bay leads the league with 16 interceptions, so ball security is the matchup to watch.

stories.text: Buccaneers at Ford Field on Sunday
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Tampa Bay (3-6) on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. Baker Mayfield is questionable with a foot injury, and rookie Jalon Daniels would start if he sits. Tampa Bay ranks first in rushing offense, led by Bucky Irving's 825 yards.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers use bye week to fix an offense that broke

stories.text: Packers head into bye after 30-10 loss to Minnesota
stories.summary: Green Bay trailed 17-0 at halftime and fell to 6-4, last place in the NFC North. Matt LaFleur called the offensive line performance bad and said the game plan should have gotten the ball out faster. The Vikings swept the season series.

stories.text: Jacobs has a broken finger, Rhyan an ankle injury
stories.summary: Running back Josh Jacobs is sidelined with a broken finger. Center Sean Rhyan missed the Minnesota game with an ankle injury and may not be ready for the Rams. The bye week gives both extra time.

stories.text: Jordan Love took a beating against Minnesota
stories.summary: Love went down eight times and took 12 hits against the Vikings. Green Bay had 57 yards of offense at halftime and four turnovers for the game. The week before, the offense scored 45 points at New England.

stories.text: 8: sacks the Vikings recorded at Lambeau
stories.summary: Seven Vikings shared the eight sacks, the most the franchise has recorded at Lambeau Field. Minnesota also took the ball away four times and outscored Green Bay 69-32 across the two meetings.

stories.text: Bye, then the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve
stories.summary: Green Bay is on its bye this week. It visits the Los Angeles Rams (6-4) on Wednesday, Nov. 25, at 8:00 p.m. ET on Netflix. The Rams are also coming off a bye.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Cousins steers Vikings to Mexico City at 7-2

stories.text: Cousins starts again with Murray out
stories.summary: Minnesota acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders after Week 9, and he opened with a 30-10 win at Green Bay. Kyler Murray (hamstring) will miss his third straight game. Cousins faces the 49ers again, having played them on Nov. 8 as a Raider.

stories.text: Murray and Addison out, Hockenson cleared
stories.summary: Quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring) and receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) are out. Cornerback Isaiah Rodgers (quad) and safety Jay Ward (knee) are questionable. Tight end T.J. Hockenson and linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel are expected to play.

stories.text: Harrison Smith keeps adding to his interception total
stories.summary: Smith picked off Jordan Love in the first quarter at Lambeau, the 41st interception of his career. The Vikings sacked Love eight times, and Smith joined a defense that forced four takeaways.

stories.text: 129: rushing yards in the win at Green Bay
stories.summary: Minnesota ran 31 times for 129 yards against the Packers, after only 12 carries in a Monday night loss to Buffalo. Jordan Mason had 59 yards on 16 carries and Aaron Jones added 47 yards and a touchdown.

stories.text: 49ers in Mexico City on Sunday night
stories.summary: Minnesota plays San Francisco (8-1) on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC, at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City. The stadium sits at roughly 7,500 feet, and Cousins has prepared with a high-altitude room.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons rest at 3-7 after dealing Bates

stories.text: Falcons sell Bates and sit on a 3-7 bye
stories.summary: Atlanta sent safety Jessie Bates III to Jacksonville for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Bates was in the last year of his contract, and the Falcons now hold four top-100 picks and plenty of cap space. They lost 35-13 to Kansas City in Week 10 and use the bye to regroup.

stories.text: London cleared of concussion before the bye
stories.summary: Coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday that Drake London passed his concussion evaluation after he left late in the Kansas City loss. London had a big day before the scare, so the bye gives the No. 1 receiver extra time to recover before the next game.

stories.text: Bijan Robinson keeps breaking runs in a loss
stories.summary: Robinson ran 16 times for 71 yards against the Chiefs as Atlanta fell behind early. He leads the team with six touchdowns, and his 12th run of 15 or more yards ties him for second in the league. The Falcons averaged 5.0 yards per carry but still threw 43 times once the game turned.

stories.text: 33: straight losses when down 10 at the half
stories.summary: Atlanta has now lost 33 straight games in which it trailed by 10 or more points at halftime. Only the Raiders, at 45, own a longer streak. The Chiefs built their lead after an offsides penalty wiped out a field goal and Kansas City scored a touchdown on the same drive.

stories.text: Falcons at Vikings after the bye
stories.summary: Atlanta is off in Week 11. The Falcons next play at Minnesota on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. It starts three straight division games, and the team wants to stop a three-game skid.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers take the NFC South lead

stories.text: Panthers beat Saints and lead the division
stories.summary: Carolina won 20-17 in New Orleans and moved a game clear atop the NFC South at 4-5. Chuba Hubbard scored both touchdowns, including the late go-ahead run. The Panthers now host Baltimore with a chance to build on the lead.

stories.text: Both tight ends questionable, Okereke out
stories.summary: Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) is out for a third straight game, and Isaiah Simmons (knee) is out too. Tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble are questionable with knee injuries. Cornerback Will Lee III (hamstring) has no designation after missing two games.

stories.text: Jaelan Phillips wrecks the Saints' protection
stories.summary: Phillips posted a season-best six pressures against New Orleans. He also had a sack and a fumble recovery. The edge rusher gave the Panthers the defensive push they needed in a three-point road win.

stories.text: 161: Hubbard's carries rank eighth in the NFL
stories.summary: Hubbard has carried 161 times, the eighth-most in the league, on a team with 222 rushing attempts. He ranks fifth in second-half rushing yards per game and averages 4.9 yards per carry on 89 second-half attempts. He gained 172 total yards against the Saints.

stories.text: Ravens visit Charlotte on Sunday
stories.summary: Carolina hosts Baltimore (4-6) on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX at Bank of America Stadium. Watch whether Hubbard keeps the ground game going and whether the tight ends play.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints chase another early deficit in Chicago

stories.text: Saints lose to Carolina and fall to 0-2 in division
stories.summary: New Orleans lost 20-17 at home to the Panthers and dropped to 3-6. The Saints have trailed in all 26 games under Kellen Moore and carry a minus-128 first-quarter point differential since the start of 2025. They now face a 7-2 Bears team.

stories.text: Five Saints out, McCoy and Fuaga among them
stories.summary: Center Erik McCoy (biceps), tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), tackle Asim Richards (knee), cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and safety Justin Reid (personal matter) are out against Chicago. Cornerback Decamerion Richardson and linebacker Pete Werner are questionable. Wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest) practiced fully Friday.

stories.text: Jordyn Tyson piles up 11 catches
stories.summary: The receiver caught 11 passes for 80 yards in the loss to Carolina, giving quarterback Tyler Shough a steady target. Carl Granderson added another sack and now has 8.5 on the season.

stories.text: 2.1: yards per carry sink the Saints
stories.summary: New Orleans averaged just 2.1 yards per carry against Carolina, a number that left the offense one-dimensional. The run game also managed 18 yards on 17 carries against Pittsburgh in Week 7.

stories.text: Saints at Bears on Sunday
stories.summary: New Orleans plays at Chicago (7-2) on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX at Soldier Field. The Saints want Shough to attack downfield, and they need a clean pocket if McCoy and Fuaga stay out.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs lean on the run and takeaways

stories.text: Bucs return from the bye as a run-first team
stories.summary: Tampa Bay sits at 3-6 but is 2-0 in the division. With Baker Mayfield hurt, the Bucs leaned on the ground game and forced turnovers to stay in games. The team opens the second half in Detroit.

stories.text: Mayfield questionable with foot and thumb issues
stories.summary: Mayfield missed three games with a dislocated thumb and then hurt his foot in the Week 9 loss to Chicago. He was limited Thursday and Friday, said he felt good, and Todd Bowles said he is trending in the right direction. Jalon Daniels starts if Mayfield sits.

stories.text: Zyon McCollum leads a ball-hawking secondary
stories.summary: McCollum has 11 pass deflections and four interceptions. His takeaways have kept a struggling Tampa Bay team within reach of opponents.

stories.text: 91.7: Bucky Irving's rushing yards per game
stories.summary: Irving averages 91.7 rushing yards per game and has eight touchdowns. He has carried the offense while the quarterback spot stayed unsettled. Mayfield has thrown for 153.7 yards per game in six starts.

stories.text: Bucs visit the 7-2 Lions on Sunday
stories.summary: Tampa Bay plays at Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The quarterback decision between Mayfield and Daniels is the key thing to watch.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Cardinals turn to a 40-year-old QB in Kansas City

stories.text: Cardinals Plan to Start Josh Johnson at Kansas City
stories.summary: Arizona is preparing for Josh Johnson to start Sunday against the Chiefs, which would make him the fourth starting quarterback of the season. Jacoby Brissett started the first eight games before a trade, Gardner Minshew tore his UCL, and rookie Carson Beck has a balky back. Coach Mike LaFleur said he will not shut the door on Beck.

stories.text: Beck Questionable With Back Injury, Two Starters Out
stories.summary: Carson Beck is questionable with a back injury that has flared up for the second time this season, and he is not expected to play. Offensive lineman Jon Gaines (ankle) and defensive lineman Zach Carter (knee) are out. LaFleur said the team is preparing for Johnson.

stories.text: Josh Johnson Is Ready for a 15th NFL Team
stories.summary: Johnson, 40, signed with Arizona the week before the game and says he feels more excited than nervous. He has made 11 NFL starts, including two with the Jets in 2021 when he threw for 621 yards and five touchdowns. Arizona is his 15th team.

stories.text: 11: Trey McBride's Streak of Seven-Catch Games Ends
stories.summary: McBride caught seven or more passes in 11 straight games before it ended in Beck's debut. He had five targets that day, his fewest since Week 16 of 2024. He still has 78 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns.

stories.text: Cardinals at Chiefs, Sunday 1:00 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Arizona (3-7) visits Kansas City (7-2) at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch who takes the first snap at quarterback and whether McBride gets his targets back. Seven games remain after this one.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams rest on a bye with four straight wins

stories.text: Rams Hit Their Bye on a Four-Game Win Streak
stories.summary: Los Angeles beat Arizona 34-6 on Nov. 15 and sits as the No. 9 seed in the NFC. The Rams scored two touchdowns in the last 1:06 of the first half to flip a 6-3 deficit. Kamren Kinchens and Wesley Bailey each picked off Carson Beck.

stories.text: Davante Adams Eyes Week 12 Return as Nacua Heads to IR
stories.summary: Adams has missed three games after surgery for a ruptured hamstring, and the Rams now hope to have him back in Week 12. Puka Nacua suffered MCL and PCL sprains and turf toe on one play and is headed to injured reserve. Kobie Turner is expected to take another IR activation spot.

stories.text: Blake Corum Runs for 100 Yards and a Score
stories.summary: Corum ran for 100 yards and a touchdown against the Cardinals. Kyren Williams has fewer than 50 rushing yards in back-to-back games, so the backfield workload bears watching after the bye.

stories.text: 9: Sacks in the Last Two Games, Up From 12 in the First Eight
stories.summary: The Rams' pass rush has picked up since Myles Garrett came off injured reserve. They had 12 sacks over the first eight games and nine over the last two.

stories.text: Bye Week, Then Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 8:00 PM ET
stories.summary: Los Angeles is off in Week 11. The Rams host Green Bay on Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 8:00 p.m. ET on Netflix. Adams and Turner are the returns to watch.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers take 8-1 mark to Mexico City at altitude

stories.text: 49ers Prepare for Altitude in Mexico City
stories.summary: San Francisco trained in Colorado Springs to get ready for Estadio Banorte, which sits 7,352 feet above sea level. The 49ers are 8-1 and 4-1 in international games. Brock Purdy leads the league at 9.0 yards per attempt.

stories.text: Mike Evans Questionable, Decision Due Saturday
stories.summary: Evans (Achilles) was limited Friday and the 49ers will decide Saturday whether he plays. Kyle Shanahan said he is a little sore but headed the right direction. Backup QB Mac Jones (illness) and linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck) are also questionable, while Christian McCaffrey and Trent Williams practiced fully.

stories.text: Brock Purdy Leads the League in Yards Per Attempt
stories.summary: Purdy averages 9.0 yards per attempt, tops in the NFL, with a 115.2 passer rating and a 70.1 completion percentage, both second. He has 20 touchdown passes. Last week he went 21 of 28 for 389 yards and three scores against Dallas.

stories.text: 584: Total Yards in the 46-40 Win Over Dallas
stories.summary: San Francisco gained 584 yards and scored six touchdowns in last week's shootout. McCaffrey piled up 223 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns. His 13 scrimmage touchdowns tie for the league lead.

stories.text: 49ers vs. Vikings in Mexico City, Sunday 8:20 PM ET on NBC
stories.summary: San Francisco (8-1) plays Minnesota (7-2) at Estadio Banorte on Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock, the first international Sunday Night Football game. Watch how the 49ers handle the altitude. Seattle visits Santa Clara the next Sunday.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks rest at 6-4 with a QB decision looming

stories.text: Lock Is 3-0, but Darnold Remains QB1
stories.summary: Drew Lock has won all three of his starts with no interceptions, and Seattle enters its bye on a two-game winning streak at 6-4. Coach Mike Macdonald still calls Sam Darnold the starter once healthy. The Seahawks are 3-4 when Darnold starts.

stories.text: Darnold Expects Full Practice Week After Bye
stories.summary: Darnold is recovering from a quad injury, and Macdonald said the team is optimistic he will get a full week of reps and play in Week 12. The extra week off from the bye gives him two weeks of recovery.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba Has 1,207 Receiving Yards
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba has 79 catches, 1,207 yards and 10 touchdowns. His yardage is more than the rest of Seattle's pass catchers combined (1,122), according to ESPN's Brady Henderson.

stories.text: 125.6: Drew Lock's Passer Rating as a Starter
stories.summary: Lock has completed 73.1 percent of his passes for 837 yards, seven touchdowns and no interceptions, averaging 9.0 yards per attempt. Darnold has 10 touchdowns and nine interceptions with a 79.5 rating.

stories.text: Bye, Then at 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 4:25 PM ET
stories.summary: Seattle is off in Week 11. The Seahawks visit San Francisco on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. The 49ers will be 8-1 or 9-1, so the defense faces its biggest test.
